main_chase_cards.name: Chikorita
main_chase_cards.why: Chikorita is the quiet opening to the Premium File story: the first Johto partner as a handled binder-card object, released exactly at the Gold/Silver threshold. It is not the loudest card in the nine-card file, but it is the first leaf of the Neo era turning over.

key_artists.name: Ken Sugimori
key_artists.why: Sugimori's Chikorita print connects the Premium File to the franchise's public design grammar: official character art becoming a collectible launch object for a new generation.

claims.text: Bulbapedia's Neo TCG Era merchandise page says the Premium File was made available on December 10, 1999 to celebrate the release of Pokemon Gold and Silver.
Bulbapedia says the Premium File includes special prints of the Generation II first partner Pokemon and their Evolutions for a total of nine cards, plus a card book.
The local source slice models one source-pinned row for this route: Chikorita source index 137.

The Premium File matters as a binder-like launch object: it packaged the Johto first-partner lines as something to hold and page through at the moment Gold and Silver were widening Pokemon beyond Kanto.
Bulbapedia's Chikorita (Neo Genesis 54) page credits the card illustration to Ken Sugimori / 杉森建.

Bulbapedia's Sugimori profile identifies him as the illustrator of the original artwork for the Pokemon games and the original artwork for all 151 Generation I Pokemon, making the credit important to how early official Pokemon visual memory travels into cards.

Bulbapedia's Chikorita page says the Japanese print was one of nine Unnumbered Promotional cards available in the Premium File released on December 10, 1999, and that it uses the Gold and Silver to a New World expansion symbol.

Agents should keep this Premium File Chikorita route separate from World Hobby Fair / Champion Road Chikorita rows, regular Neo Genesis English #54 listings, later 25th Anniversary jumbo first-partner prints, and generic Neo Premium File sealed-product lots without card evidence.

The catalog can make the Premium File route and visible-tell checklist legible, but it does not prove a seller owns the card, that a shown card is authentic, that a sealed file includes the exact card state claimed, that condition is true, that price is fair, or that the row is spendable.

narrative.human_title: Neo Era Premium File — Johto arrives as a thing you can page through
narrative.why_it_matters: The Premium File is not just a small stack of starter cards. It is Pokemon turning the page from Kanto into Johto, literally: nine special starter-family prints and a card book released on the Gold/Silver threshold. Chikorita gives that file its soft opening. The card is quiet, but the object around it is loud: a new region, a new generation, and an early lesson that Pokemon history often lives in packaging, routes, and how children were invited to hold the future before the booster era caught up.

special_identification_instructions.summary: Treat Premium File Chikorita as a specific Gold/Silver launch-file route, not as a generic Chikorita, Neo Genesis, WHF, Champion Road, or jumbo first-partner listing.
special_identification_instructions.trigger: A listing, want, scan, seller memory, or agent note says Chikorita, チコリータ, Chicorita, Premium File, Neo Premium File, Gold/Silver, Neo Genesis 54, Johto starter, starter file, or unnumbered Japanese promo.
steps: Anchor the route to Neo Era Premium File / プレミアムファイル and December 10, 1999, not the inherited local continuation-slice date.
Expect the broader product to be a nine-card Generation II first-partner family file with a card book; do not treat a loose Chikorita as a complete Premium File.
Confirm the card candidate is Chikorita / チコリータ / Chicorita and source index 137 in this local catalog route.
Look for the Japanese Premium File / unnumbered promotional route and the Gold and Silver to a New World expansion-symbol context.
Separate this row from WHF / Champion Road Chikorita prints, which use a different route and neighboring source indices.
Separate this row from English Neo Genesis #54 and from the later 25th Anniversary jumbo first-partner print.
If a seller offers a sealed Premium File, ask whether the claim is about sealed-product condition, included-card condition, or a specific Chikorita copy; those are different evidence questions.
Before any funded trade, require seller-controlled photos of the actual card or sealed product, not only a catalog image, checklist entry, or product name.

card_highlights.why_it_matters: Chikorita is the gentle one, which makes the assembly more interesting, not less. In the Premium File it is a first contact point for Johto: small, leafy, unnumbered, and packaged as part of a launch-era object that taught collectors a new region by letting them page through its starters.

artist.name: Ken Sugimori
artist.why: Sugimori's line here matters because it lets a starter feel official before it feels rare. Chikorita is not performing spectacle; it is carrying official design trust into the new region.

narrative.human_title: Chikorita — the little leaf at the Neo threshold
narrative.why_it_matters: This is the kind of card a big-price list can make look small. But if the catalog is trying to teach an agent how Pokemon was assembled, Chikorita in the first Premium File is beautiful: the new Grass starter placed into a nine-card Gold/Silver object, gentle official art carrying the promise that there is a whole new region now. It is a card about arrival. Not a trophy, not a battle prize, not the loudest holo in the room. A leaf on the first page.
